title: zk-SNARK Credentials
description: Issues credentials as zero-knowledge proofs that you satisfy a policy, without revealing the underlying attributes. A bouncer learns only 'old enough' - never your birthdate, name, or anything else on the ID.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Selective Disclosure
description: Reveals only the specific attributes a verifier needs from a credential while keeping the rest hidden and still proving authenticity. One credential can serve many verifiers, each seeing a different minimal slice.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Anonymous Credentials
description: Proves you hold a valid credential without revealing which one, so the issuer cannot track where you use it. Anonymity holds against everyone except in defined revocation cases, balancing privacy with accountability.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Range Proofs
description: Proves a hidden value lies within a range - salary above a threshold, age over 18 - without revealing the value itself. Range proofs turn private numbers into provable claims for loans, access, and compliance.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Set-Membership Proofs
description: Proves your credential belongs to an authorized set - employees, residents, subscribers - without saying which member you are. The verifier checks set membership; individual identity never enters the picture.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Policy Circuits
description: Compiles access policies into arithmetic circuits that a prover evaluates privately, outputting only grant or deny. Complex policies - role plus tenure plus training - become one proof the verifier checks in milliseconds.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Nullifiers
description: Derives a unique-per-use nullifier from each credential presentation, letting verifiers detect double-use without learning identity. Nullifiers give anonymous systems their replay protection: use once, and only once.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Revocation Registries
description: Publishes revocation status in a privacy-preserving registry where users prove non-revocation without revealing which credential is theirs. Revoked credentials stop working everywhere within the update interval, while honest users stay anonymous.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Threshold Issuance
description: Splits credential issuance across multiple authorities so no single issuer can create credentials alone or track users. A quorum must cooperate to issue, which distributes trust and removes single points of compromise.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Private Audit Trails
description: Records access decisions in an encrypted log that auditors can query in zero knowledge - proving compliance statistics without exposing individual accesses. The organization can prove 'no unauthorized access occurred' without revealing who accessed what.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Attribute-Based Proofs
description: Proves arbitrary statements about credential attributes - 'licensed in two states', 'certified after 2020' - in a single proof. Attribute-based proofs generalize selective disclosure from revealing fields to proving predicates.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Proof Aggregation
description: Combines many individual proofs into one aggregate proof a verifier checks once, slashing verification cost for busy gates. Aggregation is what makes zero-knowledge access control affordable at stadium or rush-hour scale.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Verifier Smart Contracts
description: Puts proof verification on-chain so access decisions execute as transparent, tamper-proof smart contract logic. Anyone can audit which proofs were accepted; nobody can alter the decision history.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Offline Verification
description: Verifies zero-knowledge proofs with no network connection, using cached issuer keys and revocation snapshots. Remote sites, airplanes, and disaster zones get the same access control as the connected office.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Proof of Personhood
description: Proves you are a unique human without revealing who you are, defeating Sybil attacks in voting and airdrops. Personhood proofs bind one credential per human through privacy-preserving uniqueness checks.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.
